body:
I think the example is outdated. Looking at the source code (latest ai-sdk/anthropic 2.0.23),
- `citations` is not part of `AnthropicProviderOptions`: https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/92dadc07893b0525da8d08ab31930f55f0149611/packages/anthropic/src/anthropic-messages-options.ts#L56-L84
- There is a `AnthropicFilePartProviderOptions` with `citations` in the same file. It is exported in the file but not exported in the [index.ts](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/92dadc07893b0525da8d08ab31930f55f0149611/packages/anthropic/src/index.ts). Hence, I cannot import `AnthropicFilePartProviderOptions`.
  - Also, the source code mentions it should be used for document citations, no web search

Then, there is also this PR in draft about citations: https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/5368

At least for me, the state of citations is also unclear. Based on the documentation (v5), the source code, this issue and the linked PR, I could not figure out how to use inline citations from Anthropic with setting provider options, especially when using inline citations with the [web search tool](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool#citations).

The underlying Anthropic message contains the inline citation content such as `cited_text`. You can access with `streamText` on the backend by:
1. Setting `includeRawChunks` to `true`
2. Implementing an [onChunk](https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/reference/ai-sdk-core/stream-text#on-chunk) handler that extract `TextStreamPart` of type `raw`.
3. Sending the data from backend to the frontend. Not sure what the best approach is here. You can send it as a custom data part but then you need to match the data part with the message part id manually?!

It would be nice if this citation information from the underlying anthropic message is passed to the `UIMessage` and its underlying parts, e.g. `TextUIPart.providerMetadata` so that it is available on the frontend, matching the same message part id. In other words, we should be able to use this feature with the [Inline Citation](https://ai-sdk.dev/elements/components/inline-citation) component from ai-elements.

More context that might help someone.

If you followed this [human in the loop](https://ai-sdk.dev/cookbook/next/human-in-the-loop) tutorial you may have unknowingly shot yourself in the foot. Because only the last message is evaluated for tool calling results if you send a message on top of a pending tool call you receive the error discussed here and your LLM never responds from here on out.

Disabling the user input while the last message is awaiting confirmation as the example suggests is likely not enough. To be safe you should check all past messages for non tool results either delete them or set a "skipped tool call" tool result.

body:
The underlying issue was a bug that message annotations were split between different assistant response messages. This bug was fixed by combining assistant messages into one. Also ideally UI message should be a sequence of user-assistant-user-assistant messages to make rendering in the UI easy, and combining assistant messages achieves that. Many users reporting that they needed to put hacks in place to combine assistant messages.

With this in mind, I have introduced `parts` on UI messages: https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/4670

Check out this example of using message parts with tool invocations: https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/examples/next-openai/app/use-chat-tools/page.tsx

I hope message parts are the way forward here. Please let me know if that addresses the limitations that you were facing, and if there are missing features in the new approach.

Still not clear to me why structured outputs should be enabled by default as it is not the default behavior of the models. I'd propose to adhere to the default behavior of the model providers. Also we should consider that not all models and/or providers even support structured outputs.

Can you share more details on why the ai sdk plans to defer from the defaults of all model providers?

PS: structured outputs needs to be configured separately and is just useful for very specific use-cases, but not for the standard chat-completion, afaik.
author: hopkins385

body:
@hopkins385 contrast the 2 options:

1) structured outputs are opt-in: sometimes the model will return bad completions that cannot be parsed, leading to unforeseen errors in production
2) structured outputs are opt-out: you discover immediately when your schema is incompatible (provider error during dev time) and you can opt-out. by default, the model will always return correct completions, preventing parsing errors in production. you know when you opted out and created a risk

that's why i think opt-out is preferrable
author: lgrammel

body:
By having the opt-out option you are assuming everyone prefers to configure a JSON schema and parse the output of the llm. Which means the main use-case is not chat-completion. But afaik this is not the case as the main use-case is just forwarding the tokens to the client (e.g. chat scenario).

As openai writes in their docs:
"Structured Outputs is a feature that ensures the model will always generate responses that adhere to your supplied JSON Schema, so you don't need to worry about the model omitting a required key, or hallucinating an invalid enum value." [source](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/structured-outputs)

I think "features" should always be opt-in.

body:
Confirmed this remains open in the current AI SDK v7 canary source (`b4507d5069e69e1da50cac0607d71bac2f5ac495`, June 11, 2026): `generateImage()` still accepts no `telemetry` / `experimental_telemetry` option and does not dispatch through the registered telemetry integrations.

This is now a concrete coverage gap for OpenTelemetry-based observability integrations such as PostHog's `PostHogSpanProcessor`: text generations, embeddings, and reranking can be observed through the AI SDK telemetry lifecycle, but image generation requires application-specific manual spans. That also means image cost and provider errors cannot be captured plug-and-play.

PostHog's corresponding AI SDK v7 tracking issue is PostHog/posthog-js#3674. I avoided opening a duplicate AI SDK issue because this one describes the required core change directly.

body:
> I have introduced an `onError` callback on `streamText`: https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/4729 (`ai@4.1.22`)
> 
> `streamText` immediately starts streaming to enable sending data without waiting for the model.
> Errors become part of the stream and are not thrown to prevent e.g. servers from crashing.
> 
> To log errors, you can provide an `onError` callback that is triggered when an error occurs.
> 
> ```tsx highlight="6-8"
> import { streamText } from 'ai';
> 
> const result = streamText({
>   model: yourModel,
>   prompt: 'Invent a new holiday and describe its traditions.',
>   onError({ error }) {
>     console.error(error); // your error logging logic here
>   },
> });
> ```

That was fast. Thank you!

body:
Optimal DX in this case would be for `generateObject` to always accept a valid zod schema and transform based on the provider and their specs. If `oneOf` is not supported, it should not be included in the request as such, but as instructions instead (possibly as description, not sure how it's currently implemented for models that don't support structured outputs), and the error should be thrown only if the model generated a response that could not be validated against the schema (https://sdk.vercel.ai/docs/ai-sdk-core/generating-structured-data#error-handling).

This approach is consistent with the ai sdks mission (https://sdk.vercel.ai/docs/introduction#why-use-the-ai-sdk).

body:
The underlying issue was a bug that message annotations were split between different assistant response messages. This bug was fixed by combining assistant messages into one. Also ideally UI message should be a sequence of user-assistant-user-assistant messages to make rendering in the UI easy, and combining assistant messages achieves that. Many users reporting that they needed to put hacks in place to combine assistant messages.

With this in mind, I have introduced `parts` on UI messages: https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/4670

Check out this example of using message parts with tool invocations: https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/examples/next-openai/app/use-chat-tools/page.tsx

I hope message parts are the way forward here. Please let me know if that addresses the limitations that you were facing, and if there are missing features in the new approach.

This relies on the assumption that reasoning is a single block followed by a text response, i.e. that the first text token marks the end of the reasoning process. While that's a reasonable assumption to make, the AI SDK currently allows for interleaved reasoning and text chunks, meaning that reasoning could resume after several text tokens have been sent.

For now it is probably best to use onChunk and send custom data. I'll think about how to best integrate it into the SDK.

body:
> The workaround is to use `ref` to force the component that hosts `useChat` to be recreated when it changes. Which is usually all the page. This is quite ugly but at least it works.

It is not only ugly, but won't work either. 

Consider this use case: user switches to another chat before the first one completes streaming, and then comes back to the first, and hit the stop button. 

If you force the component to rerender in order to respond to a reactive id, `useChat` will be called again, which will return a different `stop` function, which won't cancel the initial unfinished stream.

The current vue composable implementation is very largely **not** reactive, which makes it very difficult to work with. I think the API should be more native to vue instead of a mimic of the react one.

body:
The fix in #7246 helped but there's still a gap `pitstop-check` is catching:
```code
[WARN] packages/gateway/src/errors/gateway-rate-limit-error.ts:18 — 429 handled without Retry-After
[WARN] packages/provider/src/errors/api-call-error.ts:31 — CAP vs WAIT not distinguished
```
The retry layer now reads Retry-After (up to 60s), but the error types themselves don't expose the header value to callers implementing custom retry logic. So anyone wrapping the SDK — like the middleware example above — has to re-parse headers they've already seen.

The 60s cap is also the gap RickVM noted. Anthropic sometimes returns Retry-After: 600 for quota exhaustion. That's a STOP signal, not a WAIT signal — but the current logic treats it as exponential backoff.

Tool: https://github.com/SirBrenton/pitstop-check

Again, thank you all for helping us better identify this concern, which ties to a known, larger problem area with our `experimental_throttle` config option for `useChat`. Rather than ship a hacky patch fix (like the one in my PR above), we've decided to take time to explore a more robust solution in preparation for an upcoming major release.

In the meantime, you can reliably avoid the issue by:

1. Not using `experimental_throttle`
2. Explicitly adding delays before your usage of `addToolResult` / `onToolCall`!

For now, I'll be closing this issue and re-opening once we start/execute the more holistic solution!

I’ve been looking into this and started implementing the completion and structuredObject APIs in Angular. While doing so, I noticed an inconsistency between the documentation and the actual API behaviour:

According to the docs, passing an id to any of the three methods (chat, completion, structuredObject) should make them share state.

However, during v5 development, this shared state functionality was removed from the chat hook, but not from the completions or structuredObject hooks ([see commit](https://github.com/vercel/ai/commit/9ae327d7ba4176993769509b37c32369f186821d)).

I’m unsure if this is intentional. My understanding is that the goal is to let the application handle state sharing instead. If that’s the case, I think this behaviour should be consistent across all methods and the documentation updated accordingly.

IMHO, I think state sharing should be provided by the application code and not the framework and it will remove some complexity related to context management in the UI implementations.

body:
The underlying issue was a bug that message annotations were split between different assistant response messages. This bug was fixed by combining assistant messages into one. Also ideally UI message should be a sequence of user-assistant-user-assistant messages to make rendering in the UI easy, and combining assistant messages achieves that. Many users reporting that they needed to put hacks in place to combine assistant messages.

With this in mind, I have introduced `parts` on UI messages: https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/4670

Check out this example of using message parts with tool invocations: https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/examples/next-openai/app/use-chat-tools/page.tsx

I hope message parts are the way forward here. Please let me know if that addresses the limitations that you were facing, and if there are missing features in the new approach.

body:
In Electron, the proper way seems to be implementing [ChatTransport](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/ai/src/ui/chat-transport.ts) interface with [MessagePort](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/message-ports) so eventually `fetch` is not needed. The added benefit would be that the stream will be fetching from the main process and the developer console will not show the network traffic record compared to the fetch method. Keeps the prompts out of client side as well.

I am not sure if I would implement it now if the fetch method works, since in Electron it is mostly BYOK model anyway and we might not need to hide the implementation detail. If it doesn't take a long time I will post back with what I can put together in a few days.

body:
Hi @lgrammel i think you have misunderstood. The images do work as I expect.

I am not suggesting you pass the urls to the models, I was raising the inconsistency of how these values are received in the middleware. 

If message type is image and data is a URL the middleware receives the URL

If the message type is file and data is a URL then the middleware receives base64 data.

I am hoping that we can keep a reference to the downloaded pdf url in the metadata somewhere so it's accessible in the middleware
